scope.instruction: Trace the return contract of the two shared book insert routines: the slab slot index they return, its append / reuse / panic cases, and the stack-argument mode selection that does not affect it, with the two ring-append twins as the boundary.

arguments.rdi: slab collection of 0x110-byte entries: capacity +0x0, buffer +0x8, length +0x10, counter +0x18, head +0x20
arguments.rdx: caller qword copied into the event record at +0x28; not otherwise read by this routine
arguments.rcx: event collection (capacity +0x0, buffer +0x8, length +0x10) receiving one record per call
arguments.r8: pointer to the quantity accumulator qword
arguments.stack_1: mode selector: the registration arm of each twin passes 0; the append arm passes its flag qword (1 when its derivation lookup returned nonzero, else the qword at level +0x20)
arguments.stack_2: link index: the append arm passes the cached result of the previous call (the value this routine returned last time); unused in fresh mode

entry_accumulator.overflow_arm: on carry the cold block calls the helper behind slot 0x64e4ea8 with edi = 0 and the location record at 0x64b64b0, then stores the saturating sum (the recomputed sum when it does not carry, else u64::MAX)
entry_accumulator.timing: before the mode selection and all other effects

mode_selection.rule: link mode iff stack_1 == 1, stack_2 < [rdi+0x10], and the qword at [rdi+0x8] + stack_2 * 0x110 does not equal 2; every other combination falls back to fresh mode
mode_selection.flag_word: the effective flag (1 or 0) is stored into the event record at +0x8 and into the rewritten order at +0x10

fresh_mode_sources.order_+0x18: a frame slot this routine writes only on the link path (recorded, not interpreted)

event_record.grow: when length equals the capacity field [rcx+0x0], the per-twin grow slot runs on the collection before the copy

fields.source: link mode: the qword at slab buffer[stack_2] + 0xf0; fresh mode: the qword at order + 0xe0

event_record.tail: the remaining element bytes past offset 77 are not written by this routine

fields.source: link mode: stack_2; fresh mode: a frame slot written only on the link path

order_rewrite.scratch_copies: the rewritten order is copied to two frame scratch areas (the event record area after its append, and a second area past the record); neither copy is read on the return path

return_contract.value: the slab head field [rdi+0x20], loaded after the event append and the order rewrite; it is the index of the 0x110-byte slab slot that receives the order copy
return_contract.counter_before_decision: [rdi+0x18] is saturating-incremented before the head/length comparison

cases.action: when head also equals the capacity field [rdi+0x0], the per-twin slab grow slot runs first; the order copy lands in buffer[head]; length and head both become head + 1

cases.condition: head < length and the first dword of buffer[head] equals 2 (vacant)
cases.action: head becomes the qword at buffer[head] + 0x8 (the vacant slot link) and the order copy overwrites buffer[head]

cases.condition: head > length, or head < length with a first dword other than 2 at buffer[head]
cases.action: the vacant-entry panic block runs and traps with ud2

return_contract.mode_independence: the stack arguments change only the order rewrite sources and the link writes; the returned index and the slot choice never depend on them

flag_set: the element at the link index is checked (index below the current length and its first dword not equal to 2, assertion location l1/src/book/book_orders.rs:81:40) and receives 1 at +0x0 and the returned index at +0x8

then, when the rewritten order first dword equals 1, the element at the index taken from [rsp+0x10] receives 1 at +0x10 and the returned index at +0x18 under assertion location l1/src/book/book_orders.rs:89:40; otherwise the level record receives 1 at +0x0 and the returned index at +0x8
flag_clear: the level record receives 1 at +0x10 and the returned index at +0x18
then the same first-dword split applies: the second element link write, or 1 at level +0x0 and the returned index at level +0x8

level_totals.quantity: [level+0x70] += [order+0xe0] with the same checked-add shape; its overflow arm uses the second location record (also l1/src/qtys/mod.rs:831:1) and the same slot
level_totals.timing: after the link writes, before the return

vacant_entry.message: length byte 0x16 plus the 22-byte text "expected vacant entry " at the lea target 0x4339b2
vacant_entry.argument_record: two frame words: a pointer to the frame slot holding the head value, and the word loaded through slot 0x64df6c8

classes.frame_and_stack_displacements: frame size (0x408 / 0x418), the two stack-argument load displacements, and the two frame scratch offsets shift by 0x10 in shared_b
classes.event_element_size: the event record element size immediate is 0x2b8 in shared_a and 0x2c8 in shared_b (two sites)
classes.rip_relative_same_target: displacements differ but resolve to the same slot, record, message, or callee in both routines
classes.per_twin_targets: the event grow slots bind to different functions (0x59630a0 / 0x5962310); the slab grow slots differ but bind to the same function (0x43bbd40); the unwind destructor glue differs (0x5947550 / 0x5948db0)

twin_difference.verdict: the return path -- head load, counter increment, head/length decision, both slot cases, the link writes, the totals, and the rax = r13 return move -- is byte-identical in both routines; the routines are the same contract instantiated over two event record types
